actualCritique.summary: Reviewed the actual portrait and light/dark/checker PNGs, including their native 1x tiles and nearest 3x tiles. The large silver abdomen has coherent upper-left lighting, broad material planes and a readable dark plum underside. Nine red eyes are individually visible in the standing poses. Eight leg paths are largely readable, with some roots occluded by the body; the narrow far-side limbs look less substantial than the foreground limbs. No obvious accidental transparent hole or detached structural part was seen. Standing support feet maintain the ground line; raised far-side feet are consistent with perspective. Windup folds the front legs, hit recoils the head, and death visibly collapses the body. The bite and rear-leg push need clearer articulation. The skill has two large branches connected to the mouth/fang area and three recovery droplets, but recovery leaves the jaws open. Poison crouching with bubbles, stun with a drooping head and stars, and folded sleep are distinct drawn states rather than simple tints; sleep still resembles collapse, and its pair changes a forelimb more than it conveys breathing. Hands and tools are inapplicable. This is a still pose preview: actual battle contact, dash travel, animation timing and seamless playback were not observed. PNG appearance cannot establish the authoring method. This recommendation is advisory and does not record a user selection or visual approval from a geometry check.

issues.message: The far fang suddenly grows a long, nearly horizontal pale spur beyond the curled idle_a tip. Shorten this strip and redraw a tapered, outlined tip that continues the same fang curve; keep the idle changes in the jaw root rather than changing the tooth's apparent length.

The rear supporting leg remains an upright column while the abdomen stays in its idle position, so the specified rear-leg push is weak. Bend the rear knee and draw a sloping planted push leg with a connected hip; coordinate the head and front-leg advance with that push.

The two pale fangs remain separated and point largely in parallel, reading as an open jaw over the extended leg rather than a bite contact. Rotate and taper their tips toward a shared contact region, narrow the visible gape, and preserve both outlined connections to the head.

The three residual droplets read, but the jaw returns to the open idle fang shape instead of closing. Draw the two fang tips drawn inward under the mouth, with a smaller dark gape and intact roots, to make this visibly the recovery of the mouth-connected web release.

Relative to sleep_a, the long diagonal foreground limb becomes a short stepped stump while the abdomen remains fixed. Preserve that limb's length and redraw it folding at an identifiable knee. Give the sleep pair a relaxed supported head and a small coordinated abdomen/head breathing change, so it reads as resting rather than another collapse.
